newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly up on China concerns.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly up on China concerns.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Monday amid investor caution over Taiwan's economic policy towards China, brokers said.

The index ended up 9.92 points or 0.16 percent at 6,200.48. Turnover was a modest T$24.73 billion. Paper shares rose on price hike hopes and plastics rose on expected rising demand from China. Union Petrochemical rose 60 cents to T$30.2.

"Buying was cautious as investors are waiting to see the development of direct shipping link between Taiwan and China and whether Taiwan's economic policy towards China will change," said Perry Chou of Taiwan Securities.
Because of larger concerns over China policy, the market reacted little to the central bank's cut on banks' reserve requirements on Friday to boost the economy, brokers said.
"But the central bank move, which shows the government's bullish attitude, did help support the market," said Tank Hung of Yuanta Securities.
Investors are concerned about Taiwan's economic policy toward China after President Lee Teng-hui's recent comment that the government should review its China policy, brokers said.

"Other government offficials have said Taiwan's economic policy towards China remains unchanged, but investors are still concerned, awaiting further new developments," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming Securities.
Shipping shares rose hopes for direct shipping links with China, with U-Ming Marine up 80 cents to T$27.
Brokers also noted foreign funds' impact on the market.
"With Morgan Stanley set to start including Taiwan into its global indices from September 2, I don't feel pessimistic about the market's prospects," Chou said.
A 6,150-6,250 range was seen for Tuesday. -J.Peng (5080815)
